body:
## Problem

`count_periods` in `pkgs/id/src/didit/eval.rs` (lines 395–402 on main `b64288a567`) computes the `Period::Week` branch with unchecked `chrono` date arithmetic:

```rust
let monday = today - Duration::days(i64::from(today.weekday().num_days_from_monday()));
let start = midnight(tz, monday)?;
let end = midnight(tz, monday + Duration::days(7))?;
let previous_start = midnight(tz, monday - Duration::days(7))?;
```

`NaiveDate + Duration` / `NaiveDate - Duration` **panic** on overflow (chrono implements them as `checked_add_signed(...).expect("`NaiveDate + TimeDelta` overflowed")`). For a `now` in the first or last week of the representable calendar, `monday + 7 days`, `monday - 7 days`, or the Monday offset subtraction itself runs off the end of `NaiveDate`'s range and the evaluator panics — in debug *and* release builds.

This is the residual door of #7766. That fix converted the `Period::Custom` branch to checked arithmetic with the comment that "the Day/Week branches get [OutOfRange] from the calendar" — true for `Day`, which uses `succ_opt()`/`pred_opt()` (eval.rs:388–394), but not for `Week`, which uses the panicking operators. `evaluate` is documented as a pure function that "can be replayed for any past instant" (eval.rs module docs / `didit/mod.rs`), so a calendar-boundary `now` must answer `EvalError::OutOfRange`, never panic.

The same unchecked-operator pattern survives once more in the same file: `resolve_local` (eval.rs:573) computes `naive + Duration::hours(1)` when a local time falls in a DST gap; `NaiveDateTime + Duration` panics the same way at the top of the representable range. Audit it in the same pass (a checked add that falls through to the existing UTC fallback is sufficient).

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop, main `b64288a567`)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-didit-week-overflow` (laptop): the Week/Day branches and their helpers copied verbatim from `eval.rs` (file md5 `592058f89673b9202523c586c80b36fc`), built against chrono 0.4.45 (the version in `pkgs/id/Cargo.lock`), run in **release** mode:

```
NaiveDate::MAX=+262142-12-31 weekday=Mon max_now=8210266833600
NaiveDate::MIN=-262143-01-01 weekday=Thu min_now=-8334601185600
control week ordinary: Ok(((1699833600, 1700438400), (1699228800, 1699833600)))
control day  ordinary: Ok(((1699920000, 1700006400), (1699833600, 1699920000)))
week now=MAX-date noon: PANIC
day  now=MAX-date noon: Err(OutOfRange)
week now=MIN-date noon: PANIC
day  now=MIN-date noon: Err(OutOfRange)
```

Same instants, same function: `Day` returns `OutOfRange`, `Week` panics at both calendar ends. Ordinary-input controls pass for both branches.

## Why it matters

- A panic in the pure evaluator aborts whatever projection/app pass called `evaluate` — the exact failure mode #7766 fixed for `Custom`, one branch over.
- The #7766 fix comment now actively misdocuments the Week branch as calendar-guarded, so the residual is likely to survive future audits that trust the comment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `count_periods` `Period::Week` uses checked date arithmetic (`checked_add_signed` / `checked_sub_signed` or `succ_opt`-style stepping) and returns `EvalError::OutOfRange` when the week's Monday, its +7d end, or its −7d previous start is unrepresentable.
- [ ] `resolve_local`'s `+ Duration::hours(1)` shift is checked or otherwise panic-free at the representable boundary.
- [ ] Regression test mirroring `custom_period_extreme_anchor_is_out_of_range_not_a_panic_or_wrapped_window`: a Week-period expectation evaluated at a `now` on `NaiveDate::MAX` and on `NaiveDate::MIN` returns `Err(EvalError::OutOfRange)` (test fails — panics — pre-fix); an ordinary Week expectation still evaluates.
- [ ] The #7766 comment in the `Custom` branch is corrected if it still claims the Week branch is calendar-guarded.
- [ ] `cargo test` for the `didit` module passes.
